title: Returning pleasure with honest free agreement

captions.energy: Tying leisure to a compulsory response
captions.emotions: Feeling a clear proportion in participation

meaning: Honest agreement supports leisure when renewing meaningful pleasure leaves both free from reproducing an earlier response or exceeding their present wishes.
text: Renewed pleasure can acquire an unspoken condition. Judgement in the physical position of Svadhisthana describes responding to a wish to resume a meaningful pleasant activity. The Devil in energy leans towards tying leisure to the other’s compulsory reaction. Justice in emotions brings a clear sense of proportion in participation. Both may notice when an offer became a demand. Earlier joy creates no debt to repeat it today. An honest response distinguishes available agreement from yielding to preserve a pleasant picture in which the shared experience must always please equally.

For example, you offer a favourite drawing guessing game again. The other agrees to a few rounds, but a promise for the whole evening seems wanted. **Earlier enjoyment obliges neither person to greater participation today.** You can accept the named measure without secretly testing enthusiasm. Renewal already receives actual agreement. Both need neither exact repetition of the former reaction nor proof of exceptional shared interest.

The difficulty is adding conditions after the answer. You recall earlier fun and make a modest choice too costly. Proportion disappears among persuasion. Clear agreement returns enjoyment to available bounds. Both can honestly choose several rounds or refuse without punishment through coldness. The renewed experience stays an opportunity to share pleasure instead of collecting a response in payment for a valuable past. Its present scale can be freely chosen.
